solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inferior product in stock held by company

indicators.note: held by means the stock word sits inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: a stock or store of goods can be a heap, a pile

explanation.surface: A shoddy item kept in a firm's warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for a cheap, low-quality thing, so an inferior product fits.

clue.text: Indifferent — those people lacking heart for victim

parts.note: casual means indifferent

indicators.note: lacking heart means the middle letters are removed from the pronoun

parts.note: they means those people

explanation.surface: Uncaring, heartless folk overlook a victim.
explanation.walkthrough: THEY loses its heart HE, leaving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone killed or injured in an accident or war is a victim.

clue.text: I repeatedly noted new version of book

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
repeatedly means the letter I is used twice

explanation.surface: A writer keeps noting changes for a revised book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives the I twice, so IINOTED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh printing of a book is a new version of it.

clue.text: What in the Bible OT must do, giving earlier example

definitions.text: What in the Bible OT must do
definitions.meaning: the Old Testament has to come before the New Testament, abbreviated NT
a model case from the past that sets the pattern

explanation.definitionFit: An earlier case taken as a guide is the standard sense in law.

clue.text: Against having what's French and watery (Parisian soup?)

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
the Somme is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on thin French food.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear broth, a soup with a French name, hence the question mark on Parisian.

clue.text: Distressed oarsman, I'd yearn to become a sailor

indicators.note: distressed suggests the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the letters of I'd, with no apostrophe

explanation.surface: An upset rower longs to join the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest rank of seaman in the navy, a type of sailor.

clue.text: He's a tyrant? Within there lurks a lecher

indicators.note: says the answer is tucked inside the words before

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tyrant hides a lecherous nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland god of lust, hence a lecherous man.

clue.text: Endless gloom and wet weather brings animal disease

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: murk is gloom
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Bleak gloom and rain spread sickness among livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: MURK loses its end K to give MUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An infectious disease of cattle or sheep, an old word.

clue.text: Festival of the Orient lacking name

indicators.note: lacking means a letter is taken away

parts.note: eastern means of the Orient

explanation.surface: An Asian celebration with no title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian spring feast of the resurrection, a festival.

clue.text: Top banana?

parts.note: means the leading person, but read literally the finest fruit in a cluster

explanation.definitionFit: The finest of a group, figuratively the best fruit on the stem.

clue.text: The woman drinking booze by the road is a farm employee

indicators.note: drinking means the woman takes the booze inside her

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
wine is a type of booze
RD is the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A woman boozing at the roadside turns out to work on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of pigs is a traditional farm worker.

clue.text: Architectural moulding American discovered by hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
US stands for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: An American finds a piece of decorative masonry near a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A convex rounded moulding at the base of a classical column, an architectural term.

clue.text: Food from tin, meal that's horrible

indicators.note: horrible suggests the letters are made a mess of, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about a nasty tinned meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for nourishment or sustenance, so a synonym of food.

clue.text: Hurried back at speed to provide chronicle

indicators.note: back means the word for hurried is read from right to left

parts.note: ran means hurried
rate is a speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Someone rushes back quickly to deliver a report.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount events in order is to tell a chronicle of them.

clue.text: Numbers having minimal energy getting uptight

parts.note: tens are numbers
E is the physics symbol for energy, a minimal single letter

explanation.surface: Figures running low on energy become stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous and strained, a synonym for uptight.

clue.text: Coin as an item not close to hand

parts.note: something not close to hand is far away
an item is a thing

explanation.surface: A coin regarded as an object out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: A FARTHING was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: An old British coin of very low value, so an example of a coin.

clue.text: The odours upset a distinguished Greek

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Bad smells offend an eminent Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek historian, the father of history, so a distinguished Greek.

clue.text: Give line that's false to entice

indicators.note: false means the letters are not in their true order

explanation.surface: Telling a lie to lure someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax or lure by flattery, a synonym for entice.

clue.text: They cover up what has been done in operation

definitions.text: They cover up what has been done in operation

parts.words: They cover up what has been done in operation
parts.note: reads like a scandal being concealed, but means the sewing that closes a surgical wound

explanation.surface: Something hushes up the details of a covert operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical sutures close and so conceal the cut made by the surgeon.

clue.text: After end of shift worker gets drink for pet

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the next word

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: A worker has a drink after the shift ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' here means a fit of sulking, not an animal; 'After' is a link, as T comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is an old word for a sulk or fit of pique.

clue.text: Gas coming from meeting of artist and academic

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: Hot air produced when a painter meets a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive noble gas, an example of a gas.

clue.text: Professional practioner is housed in dry shelter first

parts.note: a den is a shelter

indicators.note: housed in means the word is goes inside

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means dry

explanation.surface: A professional is housed in a dry shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' says DEN comes before the rest. The clue's spelling 'practioner' is as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist is a professional who practises dentistry.

clue.text: Sin of female facing death

parts.note: end means death

explanation.surface: A woman's sin brings her face to face with death.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to commit a sin or transgress.

clue.text: Cool hit for star's devotees

parts.note: to fan is to cool
to club is to hit

explanation.surface: Fans swoon over a celebrity's cool new hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised group of admirers of a celebrity.

clue.text: Someone who endures? Son drops out subsequently

indicators.note: drops out means the letter is removed

parts.note: one who lasts is a laster

explanation.surface: An enduring person whose son leaves home later.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and subsequently both mean afterwards.

clue.text: Man put in money for bet slowly

indicators.note: put in means the man's name goes inside the stake

parts.note: an ante is the stake put up before a bet in poker
Dan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man places his stake on a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning at a moderate, walking pace, so slowly.

clue.text: English girl, not a 'bird'

indicators.note: not means the letter a is taken out of the girl's name

parts.note: Greta is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An English girl insists she isn't a 'bird', slang for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for a young woman, which the quotes play on.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron, an example of a bird.

clue.text: What 15 isn't in a narrow escape

definitions.meaning: 15 across is an old coin which is a far object; the opposite is a close object
a close shave, a situation that nearly went wrong

explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape is a close call, nearly a disaster.

clue.text: Diplomatic initiative somehow charmed English

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters arrive in some other order

explanation.surface: An English envoy charms the foreign party in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic step or political move, from French.

clue.text: Fly in groups around the centre of Cheltenham

indicators.note: the groups word and the middle letters are put one around the other
the centre of a ten-letter word is its middle two letters

parts.note: sets are groups

explanation.surface: Insects swarm around a Cheltenham town square.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'around' loosely: the groups and the centre letters are wrapped one within the other, the centre letters on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An African biting insect, an example of a fly.
